reasons.C: Closest movement: talky, chatty sentences with short punchy ones mixed in, 'Now, I...' turns and a light, gossipy tone; still missing the passage's exclamations and parentheses, but the conversational swing is nearest.
reasons.B: Confiding and good-humoured, with long, rambling sentences full of asides and a contraction, like the passage's run-ons; but the tone is more polished and Edwardian-ironic than the author's breezy slanginess.
reasons.A: Measured and formal, with balanced periodic sentences and a literary distance; it lacks the author's offhand chatter, interjections and loose clause-joining.
reasons.D: Plain modern prose with even, tidy sentences and a reflective, earnest close; it has no period colloquialism and nothing of the author's bubbling, digressive voice.
